subject: Pen test evidence & retest criteria for contract renewal
messages:
From: Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 16:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: pen test report + retest acceptance criteria for renewal

Hi Logan / Lauren,

As part of our upcoming vendor security re-review for the Q1 renewal, Security Ops at Acme Health needs the most recent third-party penetration test materials and a short note on your retest/acceptance policy. Please confirm the following:

- The date of the most recent full pen test and the firm that performed it.
- Scope (external/internal/application/authenticated tests).
- Whether you provide the full technical report + workpapers and a one-page exec summary.
- How you treat report age in procurement: do you accept reports up to 12 months old, or do you require targeted retests for anything older?
- Current remediation status for any high/critical findings (attachments are fine).

I attached our questionnaire (acme_security_questionnaire_v2.pdf) — we’ll map items to SOC 2/TSC evidence. If you can send the items by EOD Monday our review can be scheduled before the renewal call.

Thanks,
Amanda Ruiz
Sr. Security Program Manager
Acme Health

Attachments: acme_security_questionnaire_v2.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + retest acceptance criteria for renewal

Amanda — thanks for the heads up. Short answers up front, full details below.

- Most recent full third-party test: 2026-06-15 by CobaltGuard Security (independent firm). We engaged them for a full external + authenticated web application assessment.
- Scope: external perimeter, public web app (user/admin roles), OAuth token endpoints, and a targeted internal dependency scan for services in scope for SOC 2. No red-team physical/social engineering.
- Deliverables we provide to customers under NDA: full technical report (redwood_20260615_pen_test_report.pdf), executive summary, and redacted workpapers on request. We typically share the executive summary publicly and provide the technical report + workpapers under our standard NDA process.
- Report age / acceptance: our procurement baseline is 12 months for a full report. However, for renewal-sensitive customers (PHI/PCI/Sensitive-data processors) we apply a 9-month pragmatic acceptance window: if the most recent full test is older than 9 months but younger than 12 months, we will either (a) provide targeted remediation verification (retest of remediated findings) or (b) provide signed workpapers and corroborating evidence for all high/critical fixes so the buyer can accept without a full retest. If the report is >12 months old a full external reassessment is required.

- Remediation status: of two items classified as high in 2026-06, one (ID-HT-03: auth bypass vector) was fixed and retested internally on 2026-06-30 with the fix validated by CobaltGuard on 2026-07-05. The second (ID-HT-07: session fixation in legacy auth flow) has a code patch in QA with deployment planned for 2026-12-12; we have mitigation (WAF rule + token rotation) in effect. Workpapers and retest notes are attached in a redacted bundle.

I’ve attached: redwood_20260615_pen_test_report.pdf (exec summary at the top), workpapers_remediation_20260630.zip (redacted), and a short retest plan we can run if you prefer targeted revalidation. If you want the full technical report we can share under NDA — let me know and I’ll route to Marcus to execute the access.

If helpful, our acceptance matrix:
- Report age <= 9 months: full report accepted without retest.
- 9 < age <= 12 months: targeted retest of all high/critical (preferred) OR workpapers + revalidation artifacts accepted at buyer discretion.
- Age > 12 months: full retest required.

I can provide a short note mapping the report to SOC 2 TSC controls you called out.

Best,
Logan Wright
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_20260615_pen_test_report.pdf, workpapers_remediation_20260630.zip, redwood_pt_retest_plan_20261205.pdf

From: Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + retest acceptance criteria for renewal

Thanks Logan — that's helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we escalate to procurement:

1) For the 9-12 month window, does your "targeted retest" always include all high/critical findings, or do you ever accept a developer-provided remediation verification (e.g., unit test + pentester confirmation) instead of a retest? We need clarity for internal acceptance.

2) For the fixes already validated by CobaltGuard, will you provide the pentester's verification statement (signed by the vendor) as part of the workpapers bundle, or is that only in the full technical report?

3) If we do accept workpapers in lieu of a retest, what artifacts are typically included (patch diff, deployment ticket IDs, retest notes, test harness output)?

If you can confirm answers 1–3 and attach the CobaltGuard verification snapshot we can route to our procurement lead and close the evidence loop.

Best,
Amanda

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + retest acceptance criteria for renewal

Amanda — quick clarifications from our side and next steps.

1) Targeted retest scope: we require pentester revalidation for any item flagged high/critical. For medium/low, remediation artifacts + engineer verification typically suffice. We do not accept only unit tests for high/critical without vendor retest sign-off.

2) CobaltGuard verification: yes — for validated fixes we provide the pentester's short verification statement (signed PDF) and the retest summary page. That is included in the workpapers bundle we shared. If you need the vendor to sign a custom attestation for your procurement team, Marcus can coordinate.

3) Typical artifacts in a workpapers bundle: patch diff (sensitive parts redacted), deployment ticket IDs, test harness logs (sampled), pentester retest notes, and the signed verification statement. For full transparency we can also include WAF rule IDs and mitigation timestamps.

Next steps: Marcus — can you upload the signed CobaltGuard verification PDF to the shared drive link in the thread and confirm the NDA route if Acme needs the full technical report? Amanda — once Marcus uploads, I’ll send a one-page mapping to SOC 2 controls (relevant to TSC CC6 / CC7) for procurement.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pt_retest_plan_20261205.pdf
